06-01.html:
On this day of the year 97 of the martyrs (381 A.D.) one hundred and fifty fathers assembled in the second universal council upon the order of Emperor Theodosius the Great, in the City of Constantinople. Pope Timothy I (22nd Patriarch) along with some bishops attended the council on behalf of the church of Alexandria. This council assembled to judge Macedonius, Patriarch of Constantinople, Sabilius and Apolinarius for their blasphemy against God the Word and the Holy Spirit.

When these heresies became widespread, the fathers of the church were concerned about the soundness of the faith of the church, and informed Emperor Theodosius about them. He ordered the assembly of this council. When the council convened Abba Timothy asked Macedonius; "What is your belief." He replied; “The Holy Spirit was created like any other creature.” Abba Timothy debated his opinion and made it clear to him its corruption and advised him to renounce his erroneous belief. When he refused, the council excommunicated and divested him of his rank.

Then Pope Timothy asked Sabilius about his belief and he replied saying; "The Trinity has one being and one person." Abba Timothy said, "If the Trinity is one being and one person as you claimed, then the mentioning of the Trinity is groundless, and your baptism is futile, because it is in the Name of the Father, and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Then Abba Timothy advised him to renounce his erroneous belief. When he did not hearken the council excommunicated, and divested him of his rank.

Then Abba Timothy asked Apolinarius, "And you, what is your statement of faith?" Apolinarius replied saying; "The Incarnation of the Son was by uniting with the human flesh without the rational being, for His divinity replaced the soul and the mind of the human being." Abba Timothy replied saying, "God the Word united with our nature to save us, therefore if He only united with the animal body, then He did not save mankind but the animals. Humans will rise on the resurrection day with the rational soul with which there will be the judgment, and accordingly they will be granted the blessing or the condemnation. Therefore, the Incarnation would be futile. If that was the case, why did He call Himself the Son of Man if He did not unite with the rational speaking soul?" Pope Timothy advised him repeatedly to renounce his erroneous belief, but he did not hearken. The council excommunicated him as his other two friends.

Finally, the council excommunicated the three Macedonius, Sabilius and Apolinarius and all those who agreed with them. Then they completed the creed of faith from, "Yes we believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, giver of Life... to the end." They also put down many canons needed for the church then went back to their Sees in peace.

The blessing of the prayers of these holy fathers be with us all. Amen.
06-01.title: The Commemoration of the Second Universal Council in the city of Constantinople

06-01.html:
Today also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) was the martyrdom of St. Abadion, bishop of Ansena. He was ordained by Pope Peter the seal of martyrs, bishop for Ansena and he shepherded his flock with all sincerity.

When Diocletian incited the persecution against the Christians, Arianus the governor of Ansena was extremely violent in his persecution and was very versatile in the different ways of tormenting them.

He seized the St. Abadion and took him along with him in his journey to Assiut and Akhmeem to personally witness the torment of believers that he might weaken and deny the faith but he remained steadfast in his faith. The Governor ordered to bind the Saint and he took him along. The Saint went with him rejoicing as if someone going to a feast. He ordered to crucify him, two pigeons appeared above the cross and the nails were loosened and the Saint went down safely. Finally the governor ordered to behead him and he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-01.title: The Martyrdom of St. Abadion Bishop of Ansena

06-01.html:
On this day also was the consecration of the Church of St. Peter the seal of martyrs. The believers built this church west of Alexandria during the reign of Emperor Constantine the great. The church existed till shortly after the Arab conquest of Egypt.

The blessing of the prayers of this Saint be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-01.title: The Consecration of the Church of St. Peter, the Seal of Martyrs in the City of Alexandria

06-02.html:
On this day of the year 57 of the martyrs (341 A.D.) the great saint Anba Paul, the first hermit, departed. He was born in the city of Thebes and had a brother whose name was Peter.

When their father departed, they divided the inheritance between them, and Peter took the greater share for Paul was still young in age.

When they did not agree with each other, they went to the governor to judge between them. On their way, they saw a funeral procession and he was told that the deceased was one of the wealthy people of the city.

St. Paul sighed and said, "What do I have to do then with all the money of this vain world which I shall leave naked?" He said to his brother, “let us return, for I am not asking you for anything."

On their way back Paul left his brother and went on his way outside of the city. Paul found a grave where he stayed for three days praying to God to guide him to what pleases Him. His brother searched for him and when he did not find him, he was exceedingly sorry for what he had done.

The Lord sent to St. Paul an angel who walked with him to the eastern inner wilderness. He dwelt there for seventy years, during which he did not see the face of a man. He had on a tunic made of palm tree fiber. The Lord sent him a raven every day with a half loaf of bread.

When the Lord willed to reveal his holiness and godliness, He sent an angel to St. Antony (Antonius) the great and told him, "There is a man in the inner wilderness, the world is not worthy of his footsteps. By his prayers, the Lord descends rain and dew to fall on the earth, and brings the flood water of the Nile in due time."

When St. Antony heard this, he rose right away and walked a distance of one day and God guided him to the cave of St. Paul. He entered, and bowed down to each other. They sat down talking about the greatness of God. In the evening, the raven came bringing a whole loaf of bread. St. Paul said to St. Antony, "Now, I know that you are one of the servants of God. For seventy years, the Lord sent me every day a half loaf of bread, but today, the Lord is sending your food also. Now, go and bring me back in a hurry the vestment that Emperor Constantine had given to Pope Athanasius."

St. Antony went to St. Athanasius, and brought the vestment and returned to St. Paul. On his way back, he saw the soul of St. Paul carried by the angels up to heaven. When he arrived to the cave, he found that St. Paul had departed. He clothed him in the vestment and took his fiber tunic.

When he wanted to bury him, he wondered how to dig the grave. Two lions appeared to him and were shaking their heads. He knew that they were sent from God. He pointed to them the place of the grave and they dug the grave with their claws. He then buried the body, and went back to the Pope, told him what had happened and gave him the fiber tunic. St. Athanasius sent men to bring St. Paul's body to him but they could not find his grave.

Pope Athanasius used to put on the palm fiber tunic on three times a year during the Divine Liturgy of the Lord's major feasts.

The blessing of the prayers of the saint Anba Paul be with us all. Amen.
06-02.title: The Departure of the Great Saint Anba Paul, the First Hermit

06-02.html:
On this day also, the Holy Father Anba Longinus, the abbot of El-Zugag monastery, departed. He was born in Cilicia (in Asia Minor). When his mother departed he became a monk along with his father Lucianus in one of the monasteries.

After the departure of the abbot of the monastery, the monks wanted St. Lucianus to become their abbot, but he did not accept. He fled from the monastery with his son Longinus and went to Syria. They dwelt there in a church and God revealed their virtues by performing many miracles on their hands. For their fear of the glory of men Longinus took the permission of his father to go to Egypt.

He went to the monastery of El-Zugag to the west of Alexandria. He pursued a life of godliness, piety and asceticism. After the departure of the abbot, the monks made him abbot against his will. Shortly after, his father Lucianus came, and they worked in making the canvas sails of boats, and sold them to support themselves. God performed many miracles on their hands.

Father Lucianus departed in peace, and shortly after, his son Longinus departed also on this day.

The blessing of the prayers of these two saints be with us all, and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-02.title: The Departure of St. Longinus, Abbot of El-Zugag Monastery and his father St. Lucianus

06-03.html:
On this day, St. James, the ascetic monk, departed. This father denounced the world since his young age. He dwelt in a cave for fifteen years, during which he exerted himself with long fasting and frequent prayers and he never left the cave all that time.

The devil was envious of him so he enticed a wicked woman who decorated herself and went to him. She tried to seduce him to commit sin with her. But he preached to her, and reminded her of the torment of the fire of hell, judgment and the eternal punishments. She repented and went back to the city thanking God Who granted her to return from the way of eternal death to the way of eternal life.

God performed many miracles by his hands. When the Lord willed to relieve him from the toil of this futile world he fell ill for a short time then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-03.title: The Departure of St. James, the Monk

06-03.html:
On this day also St. Hedra, of the Rock of Banhadab, departed. He was the first monk to settle on the rock of Banhadab for his love of the solitary life rejecting the waves of this vain world.

During his days, there was an ascetic man who was known for his spiritual deeds and virtues whose name was Juda. This Juda because of his simplicity had disbelieved in the resurrection of the bodies. God the lover of mankind did not will for this hermit to perish so He guided him to go to St. Hedra. He told the Saint of his disbelief. He was converted from his error by St. Hedra who exhorted and explained to him this doctrine. He told him that the Lord Jesus Christ was the first fruits of those who have fallen asleep. St. Juda believed and thanked St. Hedra for he had enlightened him.

St. Hedra became well known for his godliness and piety and the Lord wrought many miracles by his hands. Many came to him to receive his blessing and prayers. This father endured the life of the wilderness and asceticism. He became ill for a short time then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-03.title: The Departure of St. Hedra, of the Rock of Banhadab

06-04.html:
On this day, St. Agabus, one of the seventy disciples, was martyred. They were chosen by the Lord to go before Him to preach the word of life. St. Agabus was with the twelve disciples in the upper room of Zion on the day of Pentecost.

God granted him the gift of prophecy, as the Acts of the Apostles tells us, "And as we stayed many days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea. When he had come to us, he took Paul's belt, bound his own hands and feet, and said, 'Thus says the Holy Spirit, so shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt, and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles."' (Acts 21: 10-11)

He also prophesied about a famine which was fulfilled during the time of Claudius Caesar.

This apostle preached the gospel to many countries converting many of the Jews and the Greeks to the faith of the Lord Christ.

Finally the Jews of Jerusalem seized, and scourged him severely then tied a rope around his neck and dragged him outside the city where they stoned him until he delivered up his pure spirit in the hand of the Lord whom he loved. Thus he received the crown of martyrdom. A light came down from heaven to his body. When a Jewish woman saw that light she cried saying, "Truly this man was righteous." Then she shouted in a loud voice saying, "I am a Christian." They stoned her also; she departed in peace and received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of the prayers of this apostle be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-04.title: The Martyrdom of St. Agabus, One of the Seventy Disciples

06-05.html:
On this day, the church celebrates the commemoration of the relocation of the relics of the forty-nine martyrs of the wilderness of Shiheet to their church in the monastery of St. Macarius.

Pope Benjamin I, 38th Patriarch, repeated their shrouding, embalming, and re-burying them in the middle of the church. He also established this day a feast for relocating their bodies.

The pure relics of these Saints remained in this church until it fell apart. The monks kept their bodies in one of the cells till the time when el-Moalem Ibrahim El-Gohary built for them a church in the year 1732 A.D. Their bodies still exist till present time in this church in the monastery of St. Macarius the great. The church is called the church of the elders.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-05.title: The Commemoration of the Relocation of the Relics of the Forty-Nine Elders of the Wilderness of Shiheet

06-05.html:
On this day also of the year 178 A.D., Pope Agrippinus, the 10th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This Holy Father was born in Alexandria. He was pure, saintly and feared God. He was ordained a priest for the church of Alexandria.

When the blessed father Pope Celadion, the 9th Patriarch, departed, he was chosen patriarch. By the grace of God, he took over the apostolic throne, preaching the word of God, teaching the principles of the faith, and guarding the flock.

He did not possess any silver or gold, except what met his basic needs. He was a contemporary of the persecution of Emperor Marcus Aurelius, during which he supported the faithful exhorting them moreover he preached to the heathens and converted many of them to the faith. When he completed his good endeavor, he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-05.title: The Departure of St. Agrippinus, 10th Pope of Alexandria

06-05.html:
Today also the saint Anba Bishay the founder of the red monastery, west of Souhag, departed. This Holy Father was born in the village of Absounah. In his young age, he worked in in-appropriate jobs but because of the Love of God for him, He brought upon him a sickness during which he saw a vision. In this vision he saw the places of torment. He sighed, cried and raised his eyes to heaven saying, “My Lord and God, if you heal me I will repent and worship you with all my heart.

When he was cured a noble thought pondered in his heart, so he started to renounce this world and forsake everything even the sheep that he tended and went up the mountain. On his way, he met Anba Pigol (Bajoul), the uncle of St. Shenoute the Archimandrite, and dwelt with him on mount Adribah. They practiced many worship and ascetic works without boredom, fasting and vigils. They suffered from the enemy many temptations but the Lord saved them from his snares.

The account of Anba Bishay became well known in all the land of Egypt. He put down many discourses and useful teachings for the monks and the laity. One time he fasted for a whole month and the deeds of people were uncovered before him.

During these days, Anba Shenouda went up to his uncle Anba Pigol and the angel of the Lord directed him to put on his nephew the Holy Eskeem. He put on him the Eskeem in the presence of Anba Bishay. The three joined together in worship and asceticism. They made for themselves dwellings in the mountain and built a church after the name of the Virgin Mary.

When Anba Bishay finished his good endeavor, departed in peace and the saint Anba Shenouda shrouded him. He buried him in the monastery which was named after him and known by the Red Monastery, west of Souhag. Anba Shenouda wrote down his biography and asceticism. He called him Peter for what he saw from his endurance of hardships as the rock.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-05.title: The Departure of the Saint Anba Bishay the Founder of the Red Monastery

06-05.html:
On this day also the saint Anba Apollo who was like the angels, the companion of St. Abib departed. They were of the fourth century saints. He was born in the city of Akhmeem. He resembled his parents in piety since his young age. He practiced life of asceticism and was inclined to the solitary life. He spent his time in studying the Holy Bible, contemplating and praying.

He had a close friend called Abib and they were in agreement in thought and had the same monastic aspiration. Apollo went to one of the monasteries where he dwelt in seclusion in a cell practicing a life of fellowship with God. He met his friend Anba Abib from time to time and was present at the time of his departure. The Holy Father Anba Apollo departed in a good old age.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-05.title: The Departure of St. Apollo, the Companion of Anba Abib

06-05.html:
Today also marks the martyrdom of St. Hippolytus, Pope of Rome. He was a perfect and righteous man, so they chose him for the Roman See after the departure of Father Augius (Hyginus Pius). This was in the first year of the enthronement of Abba Celadion, 9th Patriarch of Alexandria.

Pope Hippolytus constantly taught his people and defended the Orthodox faith. When Claudius Caesar (Antonius) the Roman Emperor heard of him, summoned the saint and asked him to worship the idols. When he refused, he ordered to torture him. They tortured him severely then tied a heavy stone to his feet and threw him into the sea. He departed in peace and received the crown of martyrdom.

On the following day, one of the faithful found the body of the saint floating above the water, and the stone was still tied to his feet. He took him to his home, shrouded him with expensive shrouds, and buried him.

This father left a great wealth of teachings and 38 church canons that are still in use.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-05.title: The Martyrdom of St. Hippolytus, Pope of Rome

06-05.html:
On this day also was the departure of the saint Aba-Noub (Apanoub) who is known as the Owner of the Golden Fan.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-05.title: The Departure of St. Aba-Noub, the Owner of the Golden Fan

06-06.html:
On this day the saints Cyrus (Abakir), John, the three virgins, and their mother were martyred in the city of Alexandria.

Abakir (Cyrus) was born in Alexandria to godly parents who raised him up with a Christian upbringing. He grew loving God and the church. He learned the medical profession and became known for his knowledge, godliness and love for the poor. They accused him before the governor that he was healing the people with sorcery and magic. He ordered to arrest him in spite of his knowledge of all the services that he offered freely to the people. Cyrus fled to the eastern desert where he joined the hermits, lived among them and served them.

However, John was a high ranking officer in the army of the countries in Mesopotamia. He was a pious Christian inclined to the ascetic life and worship. When he heard about Abakir (Cyrus), he left the military service, went to visit the holy places in Jerusalem, and then went to the eastern desert where St. Cyrus was. John met him, and saluted each other, and John dwelt nearby Cyrus. He took him as a teacher and they became spiritual brothers.

When Diocletian incited the persecution against the Christians, Alexandria became a stage for the torment and torture of the believers. The soldiers of the Governor seized a Christian woman called Athanasia (which means: the immortal) and her three virgin daughters. Theeodora (which means: the gift of God), Theopisti (which means: the faith of God) and Theodosia (which means: the glory of God). They led them bound for trial and torture to an area called Kanoub, east of Alexandria.

When St. Cyrus (Abakir) heard, while he was in the desert, of the arrest of Athanasia and her daughters, he had compassion for them, for he had known them from before. He was concerned that torture might weaken their faith. He decided to go down to Alexandria to stand beside them. His spiritual brother John went down with him. As they entered Alexandria they went to Kanoub to encourage Athanasia and her daughters.

Some wicked men informed the Governor of the arrival of Cyrus and John. He ordered to arrest, try, and torment them with severe tortures. He also ordered to behead Athanasia and her three daughters before Abakir (Cyrus) and John to frighten them. Nevertheless, they became more steadfast in their faith and longed also for receiving the crown of martyrdom. After a long series of tortures, the Governor ordered to behead them thus they received the crown of martyrdom. That was in the area called Kanoub which was called later on Abu-Kir in reference to the saint Abakir.

St. Julius of Aqfahs came with his men, carried the bodies of the martyrs and buried them in a tomb nearby the church of St. Mark in Alexandria and he also wrote down the story of their strife and martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-06.title: The Martyrdom of Sts. Cyrus, John, the Three Virgins and Their Mother

06-06.html:
Today also of the year 1079 of the martyrs (1363 A.D.) Pope Mark (Marcus) IV, 84th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was a native of the city of Qalyub and became a monk in the Shahran monastery by the name the monk Ghabrial. He was a righteous monk, knowledgeable and godly.

After the departure of Pope Peter V, the bishops and the archons (lay leaders) convened and they chose this monk. He was consecrated Patriarch on the 8th of Thoout, year 1065 A.M. (1348 A.D.) by the name Pope Mark IV.

During his days a severe persecution befell the Copts, some of the churches were destroyed and the monasteries were ruined. The country faced many difficulties. The Pope was imprisoned and the Christian King of Ethiopia had to intervene to release the Pope.

Finally after thankfully enduring the Lord willed to relieve him from the toils of this world, he delivered his pure soul in the hand of the Lord and was buried in Shahran monastery.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-06.title: The Departure of Pope Mark (Marcus) IV, 84th Patriarch of Alexandria

06-06.html:
On this day also the Holy Father Anba Zanofios, departed. He was the abbot of a large community of monks in the region of el-Mara’igh, district of Akhmeem. He was known for asceticism and worship. He taught his children the monk’s virtues, worship and the fear of God. He also established a convent for the virgins, put in charge a righteous mother and sent them epistles that explained the commandments and monastic rules.

When he finished his good endeavor departed in peace and was buried in his monastery. God wrought many signs from his pure body.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-06.title: The Departure of St. Zanofios

06-07.html:
On this day of the year 445 of the martyrs (729 A.D.), the Holy Father Abba Alexandros II, 43rd Pope of Alexandria, departed. He was born in the village of Bana, El Mahalla el-Kobra. He was raised on piety, godliness and love of solitary life. He became a monk in the monastery of Pateron, the monastery of the fathers, which was also known as El-Zugag monastery by the name of the monk Alexandros. He lived a life of asceticism, fasting and prayers until the fame of his virtues became well known, so the fathers ordained him a priest for the church of the monastery.

When the apostolic throne became vacant by the departure of Pope Simeon I, they unanimously agreed to choose the monk Fr. Alexandros. They consecrated him Patriarch on the 30th of Parmoute, year 420 A.M (704 A.D.)

The early days of his pontificate were tranquil however the devil incited the war against the church. The ruler of the country mistreated the Christians and seized the Patriarch and did not release him until he collected for him three thousand Dinars. The governorship of this ruler did not last long moreover the next ruler was even worse than him. The state of the Christians deteriorated more. The fines and difficulties were repeated under the next following four rulers. Hardships were from within the church and also from the Chalcedonians. The Pope endured all these pains praying and supplicating the Lord until he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-07.title: The Departure of St. Alexandros II, 43rd Pope of Alexandria

06-07.html:
On this day also of the year 458 of the martyrs (742 A.D.) St. Theodorus (Theodor) I, 45th Pope of Alexandria, departed. This Holy Father became a monk by the name Tadros in a monastery nearby Mariot. He became a disciple under the guidance of a holy elder monk called Yoannis (John). Abba Yoannis was inspired by the Holy Spirit that his disciple Tadros would become one day a Patriarch. Abba Yoannis told the people in the church about his vision.

The monk Tadros struggled in his worship and was perfect in his humility and meekness. When the apostolic throne became vacant by the departure of Pope Cosma I, the bishops and lay-leaders convened. They remembered the prophecy of Anba Yoannis so they brought the monk Fr. Tadros from the monastery against his will. They consecrated him Patriarch on the 1st day of Epep, year 446 A.M. (730 A.D.)

After his enthronement, he took interest in the pastoral care of his flock. The church during his days enjoyed a good deal of rest although he faced many hardships for he witnessed the calamities brought by the rulers. He patiently endured what he witnessed nevertheless the church continued to grow spiritually until he completed his good strife and departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-07.title: The Departure of St. Theodorus (Theodore), 45th Pope of Alexandria

06-08.html:
On this day the church celebrates the feast of presenting the Lord Christ into the temple. It is one of the minor feasts of the Lord. On the fortieth day of the birth of the Lord Christ, His mother the Virgin St. Mary took Him along with St. Joseph the carpenter and went with Him to the temple, to do for him according to the custom of the law and to offer on His behalf the required sacrifice according to their ability. Because of the poverty of the Virgin and Joseph, they offered the sacrifice of the poor which was two young pigeons.

The Virgin St. Mary who conceived by the Holy Spirit and gave birth to the Savior of the world with all purity, submitted to this law to exercise the virtues of humility, obedience to the law, and for us to follow her example. And to follow her Son the Lord Jesus Christ who obeyed the law of the Old Testament with all humility before He established the law of the New Testament.

And behold in the Temple there was an old priest whose name was Simeon, and this man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. And when the parents brought in the Child Jesus, to do for Him according to the custom of the law, Simeon took Him up in his arms and blessed God and said: “Lord, now You are letting Your servant depart in peace …” Then Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, “Behold this Child is destined for the fall and rising of many in Israel and for a sign which will be spoken against (which is the sign of the Cross) yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul also (the sword of grief at the crucifixion of Christ).

Now there was one, Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, and coming in that instant she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of Him to all those who looked for redemption in Jerusalem. So when they had performed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth. And the child grew and became strong in spirit, filled with wisdom; and the grace of God was upon Him.

The blessing of our Lord Jesus Christ who laid down for us the way of salvation be with us all. Amen.
06-08.title: The Feast of Presenting the Lord Christ to the Temple

06-08.html:
On this day also St. Simeon the elder departed.

Simeon was one of the seventy elders who translated the Old Testament from the Hebrew language to the Greek in Alexandria. That was by the order of Ptolemy Philadelphus, king of Egypt.

When Simeon was translating the verse from Isaiah the prophet (7:14), "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel," he was afraid to translate that a virgin would conceive, because the King might mock him and accuse him of ignorance. He wanted to translate the virgin as a "young lady or damsel".

He became doubtful saying to himself it is impossible for a virgin to conceive. God revealed to him in a vision that he would not die before he would see Immanuel born of a virgin. This was fulfilled and he lived about three hundred years until the Lord Christ was born from the Virgin Mary without a human seed but by the Holy Spirit. Simeon was well advanced in age and his sight dimmed.

When he came by the Spirit into the temple and carried the Divine Child in his hands, his sight came back, and the Holy Spirit told him, "This is the child that you have been waiting for." He blessed God and said, "You are letting Your servant depart in peace according to Your Word, for my eyes have seen Your salvation which You have prepared before the face of all peoples." (Luke 2:28-32) He blessed Joseph and Mary and prophesied for them about the future of the Child and about the pains that the Virgin would suffer and in the same day he departed in peace.

The prayers of this righteous man be with us all. Amen.
06-08.title: The Departure of St. Simeon the Elder

06-08.html:
Today, the Church commemorates the contemporary martyrs of the Coptic Church, foremost among them the 21 Coptic martyrs in Libya. On this day in 2015 AD, a terrorist group in Libya released a video depicting their execution by beheading in the city of Sirte, on the shores of the Mediterranean Sea.

In recent years, many children of the Coptic Church have been martyred in various regions of Egypt, joining the chorus of the martyrs in Heaven. In recognition of their sacrifice, the Holy Synod, under the leadership of His Holiness Pope Tawadros II, has designated the 8th of Meshir as a feast and commemoration day for all the martyrs of the Coptic Church in its modern era.

We celebrate them to honor and to keep their memory and to draw blessings from their lives, as living examples of divine love and steadfast faith. This aligns with the wisdom that says, "You may move a mountain from its place, but you cannot move Copts from their faith."

We are called to consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith, as our teacher St. Paul advises in his epistle to the Hebrews (Hebrews 13:7).

The blessing of their prayers be with us, and glory be to God forever, Amen.
06-08.title: The Commemoration of the Contemporary Martyrs of the Coptic Church

06-09.html:
On this day of the year 174 of the martyrs (458 A.D.) the blessed father Anba Barsauma, the father of the Syrian monks, departed. This Holy Father was born in the city of Samosata, in Syria. A holy man prophesied about him before his birth saying to his parents, "There shall go forth from you a righteous fruit, whose fame shall spread out everywhere."

This prophecy was fulfilled, when Barsauma grew up, he left his parents and went to the river Euphrates where he dwelt with a holy man called Abraham. Afterwards, he lived in solitude on the mountain praying and fasting with austere asceticism. Many disciples gathered around him. The water of that place was salty, and with the prayers of the saint it became sweet. God wrought through him many miracles. A famine befell this country and God lifted it up by his prayers.

St. Simeon the Stylite visited him and they blessed each other. This saint was well known for his resisting the heresy of Nestorius. He attended the Universal Council at Ephesus in the year 431 A.D. by an invitation of Emperor Theodosius the Less, who greatly honored him.

When Emperor Marcian convened the Chalcedonian council, the fathers asked the Emperor not to invite St. Barsauma to the council, for they knew of the grace that was in him. When the council agreed on the two natures of Christ, St. Barsauma resisted these heretical teachings and many hardships befell him from the Chalcedonians.

This Holy Father knew the day of his departure. He gathered his disciples, blessed them and commended them to steadfast in the Orthodox faith and departed in peace.

At the time of his departure, a pillar of light appeared at the door of his cell. They shrouded and buried him with great honor.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-09.title: The Departure of St. Barsauma, the Father of the Syrian Monks

06-09.html:
On this day also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) St. Paul the Syrian was martyred. His family relocated from Syria and settled in the City of Ashmunain. From working in trading his father gained a great wealth. God granted them this saint and they raised him in a true Christian upbringing, growing in godliness and loving the Lord from all his Heart.

After the death of his parents, the saint prayed to God to guide him in the way that pleases Him. The Lord sent His angel in a vision and made it known to him that he will receive the crown of martyrdom. The saint rejoiced and was comforted. He distributed all his money to the poor and the needy.

The saint arose right away and went to the governor of Ansena (Antinoe) and confessed the Lord Christ before him. The Governor ordered him stripped naked, beaten with whips, and to place burning torches to his sides. The saint was not afraid and the governor tried again to entice him with money, but the saint told him, "My parents left me a fortune of gold and silver, and I rejected them for the sake of the love of my Lord and God Jesus Christ. So why should I look to your money now?"

The Governor became angry and he tormented him with different kinds of tortures. However the Lord healed and strengthened him. Later on the governor ordered him placed with venomous serpents which did not harm him.

When the governor was weary of torturing him he took the saint with him to Alexandria and imprisoned him. In prison, he met his two friends the saints Esi and his sister Thecla and their soul rejoiced.

When the Governor decided to return to Ansena, he ordered to behead St. Paul thus he received the crown of martyrdom. The faithful came, took his body, shrouded it and buried him with great honor.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-09.title: The Martyrdom of St. Paul the Syrian

06-09.html:
Today also marks the martyrdom of St. Simeon.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-09.title: The Martyrdom of St. Simeon

06-09.html:
Also on this day of the year 186 of the martyrs (470 A.D.) was the departure of St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria. This saint was born in Alexandria, an only child to godly and wealthy family. They raised her with a true Christian upbringing. She learnt from her parents the fear of God and the charity for the poor and the needy.

When she was eighteen years old, she left her home, wearing the attire of men and went to one of the monasteries. The abbot of the monastery accepted her and put her up in a solitary cell. She devoted herself to fasting, prayers and austere asceticism which changed her appearance.

Her father visited the monastery often asking the monks to pray for him for the Lord to grant him peace and comfort for his heart. Euphrosyne recognized him but he did not know her, however she received and encouraged him. He found consolation from the words of grace that she spoke to him.

Euphrosyne became ill and she knew the day of her departure. When her father came to the monastery, she revealed her identity to him and told him that she was about to depart. He embraced her crying however she encouraged and consoled him then she departed between his arms.

He was very much moved and agreed with his wife to forsake the vanity of the world. He sold all his possessions and distributed the money to the churches and the poor. His wife joined one of the convents and he dwelt in the cell of his daughter in the monastery for ten years then departed in peace.

The blessing of St. Euphrosyne be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-09.title: The Departure of St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria

06-10.html:
On this day St. Philo, bishop of the Persians, was martyred by the hand of the Persian Emperor.

He tried to force him to worship fire and to kneel to the sun that the Persian Emperor worshiped. When St. Philo refused to obey the orders of the emperor and stood fast in his faith in the Lord Christ, the emperor tormented him with different kinds of tortures. Finally he ordered to behead him with the sword thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-10.title: The Martyrdom of St. Philo, Bishop of the Persians

06-10.html:
On this day also, St. Justus, the son of Emperor Numerian, was martyred. He was a prince and a high ranking army commander. When he returned victoriously from the war against the Persians, he found that his father had died; Diocletian had married his sister and became emperor.

When the nobles of the empire met together to enthrone Justus emperor, he refused, for he preferred the heavenly kingdom over the earthly. After a while Diocletian abandoned the faith of the Lord Christ and worshiped the idols. When Justus objected to what Diocletian had done, he seized him, his wife Theoclea and his son Abali and sent them to Alexandria to be tortured there away from their country and their people.

When they arrived to Alexandria, the governor tried to persuade them to worship the idols. They refused declaring their steadfastness in their faith in the Lord Christ. He sent St. Justus to Antinoe (Ansena), Abali, his son, to Basta and Theoclea to Sa el-Hagar. The rulers tortured them then beheaded the three saints, and they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-10.title: The Martyrdom of St. Justus, the Son of Emperor Numerian

06-10.html:
On this day also of the year 166 of the martyrs (450 A.D.) the great saint, ascetic and scholar Anba Isidore of Pelusium (El-Farama), departed. He was born in Alexandria in the year 370 A.D. to a large family. He was related to the saints Pope Theophilus, the 23rd patriarch of Alexandria and Pope Cyril I, the 24th Patriarch. His parents raised him up with a Christian upbringing and taught him the church subjects.

When he grew he learnt the Greek language and its literature which he excelled in and surpassed many. He became a scholar in many subjects, Philosophy, History and Logic however he was a humble ascetic.

He fled away from the glory of the world and became a monk in one of the monasteries in the region of el-Farama. Then he moved to the region of Pelusium to live there a life of solitude and asceticism. His monastic conduct was purely evangelical inclined to simplicity caring for the inward adornment of the soul with virtues.

He was interested in his seclusion to interpret the Holy Scriptures. He commented on many books of the Old and New Testaments. He also wrote powerful epistles to many of the emperors, patriarchs, bishops and monks. These epistles estimated to be about two thousand. The gifts of the Holy Spirit were abundantly clear in his writings. When he reached a good old age departed in peace and went to the Lord whom he loved.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-10.title: The Departure of St. Isidore of Pelusium

06-11.html:
On this day of the year 1240 of the martyrs (1524 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Yoannis XIII (John), the 94th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This saint was born in the city of Sedfa. He was a godly man, charitable to the poor and the needy. He became a monk in the monastery of the Virgin St. Mary, el-Moharraq. He lived a pious monastic life.

After the departure of Pope Yoannis XII, the bishops and the lay leaders of the people unanimously agreed to choose the monk John el-Moharraqy (John el-Masry, the Egyptian) to be ordained patriarch. He was consecrated on the 15th day of Meshir, year 1200 of the martyrs (1484 A.D.). He shepherded the flock of God with the best of care.

During his days there was a Coptic episcopate on the island of Cyprus and also was the return of the relics of the great martyr St. Philopateer Mercurius (Abu-Saifain) to his church in Old Cairo.

Pope Yoannis remained on the apostolic throne struggling to improve the standing of his church for forty years accomplished in them many renovations, improvements and wrote many spiritual books.

Then he departed in peace and was buried in the church of the Virgin Mary in Haret Zuweila which was the Papal residence at that time.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-11.title: The Departure of Pope Yoannis XIII (John), 94th Patriarch of Alexandria

06-11.html:
On this day also, St. Fabianus, Pope of Rome, was martyred. This father was a righteous scholar. He was ordained bishop for the City of Rome. He taught his people and guided them in the way of Christian perfection.

When Emperor Decius incited persecution against the Christians, many were martyred at his hands. The Emperor was informed that St. Fabianus was confirming the Christians in their faith which hindered worshipping the idols. He brought Fabianus to Ephesus and commanded him to raise incense to the idols but he refused. The Emperor tormented him with many severe tortures for a long time. Finally he ordered to behead him with the sword thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

Pope Fabianus stayed on the apostolic throne for twelve years.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-11.title: The Martyrdom of St. Fabianus (Fabrianus), Pope of Rome

06-12.html:
On this day the church celebrates, the monthly commemoration of the honorable Michael the Archangel, the intercessor of mankind.

His holy intercession be with us all. Amen.
06-12.title: The Commemoration of the Honorable Archangel Michael

06-12.html:
Also on this day, St. Gelasius, the ascetic, departed. This Holy Father was born to Christian parents, who brought him up with a Christian upbringing. They taught him the church subjects, and he was ordained a deacon.

He became a monk in the wilderness of Shiheet. The angel of the Lord guided him to a place in the inner wilderness where some monks who desired the solitary life gathered around him. St. Gelasius became a teacher and guide for them. He worked in transcribing the Holy Scriptures.

He loved everyone and forgave those who trespassed against him. He reached a high degree of holiness to the extent that he raised a dead man.

His life was a good example for everyone. After a long struggle in the monastic life, asceticism, worship and guiding the brethren, he departed in peace and gained the eternal rest.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-12.title: The Departure of St. Gelasius, the Ascetic

06-13.html:
On this day, St. Sergius, his father, mother, sister and many others with them were martyred. This saint was born in the City of Atripe to pious parents who raised him with Christian principles.

When he was 20 years old, he thought about the vanity of the world and the eternal happiness, so he rose and went to Cyprian, the governor. He professed his faith in the Lord Christ before him. The governor commanded to torture and then imprisoned him.

At night he saw in a vision the habitations of the righteous, his soul was comforted, and the Lord healed him from his wounds.

Ohios, the captain of the soldiers, took charge of torturing St. Sergius. He ordered to skin him and to rub his wounds with salt and vinegar, then crush him with the pressing wheel (Hinbazeen), to pull his nails out and to place him on an iron bed over a blazing fire. However the Lord strengthened and healed him. When Ohios, the commander, was weary of torturing him he ordered to behead him.

At that time his father, mother, sister and many others with them came. When they saw him tied up with the bridle of a horse dragging him to the place of execution, they protested the soldiers for their extreme cruelty. The captain ordered to behead them all and they all received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-13.title: The Martyrdom of St. Sergius of Atripe, His Father, Mother, Sister, and Many Others with Them

06-13.html:
On this day also of the year 252 of the martyrs (536 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Timothy III, the 32nd Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This saint was born in the city of Alexandria. He studied the church subjects and excelled in them. He was ordained a priest for the church of St. Mark in Alexandria. The fame of his holiness, knowledge, and steadfastness in the Orthodox faith became well known.

When the apostolic throne became vacant after the departure of Pope Dioscorus II, the bishops, priests, and lay leaders (Archons) convened and prayed entreating God to guide them to whomever worthy of this rank. The Holy Spirit inspired them to choose the priest Timothy. He was consecrated Patriarch on the first day of Hathor, year 235 of the martyrs (518 A.D.).

He followed the same manner of his predecessors by sending a fellowship epistle to his brothers the bishops of the East. They all replied declaring their joy for the perpetuity of peace and love between them.

This father suffered many hardships for preserving the Orthodox faith. Emperor Justin I was an advocate of the Chalcedonian council and called for a council to excommunicate St. Severus, Patriarch of Antioch. Pope Timothy refused to attend this council consequently the emperor ordered to exile him. When the faithful opposed the execution of his order he killed a large number of them. They arrested Pope Timothy and he was exiled for three years.

After the return of Pope Timothy from exile they continued to pursue him and St. Severus from town to town and from a monastery to another. Wherever they went, they commended the people to steadfast in the Orthodox faith. Finally they took refuge in a monastery away from the reach of the soldiers. They wrote epistles to their people to comfort their hearts and to strengthen their resolve.

Pope Timothy persevered on teaching his flock with the written word directing the affairs of the church in the middle of all these hardships. He persisted in his continuous spiritual struggle until he departed to the place of perpetual peace after he had been on the apostolic throne for about 17 years.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-13.title: The Departure of St. Timothy III, the 32nd Patriarch of Alexandria

06-14.html:
On this day the Holy Father St. Severus, Patriarch of Antioch, departed. This saint was born in the year 175 of the martyrs (459 A.D.) in the city of Sozopolis in Asia Minor. His parents raised him up with a Christian upbringing and taught him the religious and secular subjects. After he finished his studies of Philosophy in Alexandria he went to Beirut to study law and he excelled and everyone expected for him a great future.

Severus grew in spiritual life and an ascetic prophesied about him that he would be Patriarch of Antioch, teacher of Orthodoxy and its defender. Later on he became a monk in the monastery of St. Romanus and the fame of his virtues and knowledge became well known.

When the Patriarch of Antioch departed, the bishops and the people had a consensus to ordain him the Patriarch of the city in the year 512 A.D. The universal church was illuminated by his teachings.

When Emperor Justin I, who was Chalcedonian in faith, reigned, he called upon this Holy Father and gave him great honors to persuade him to adopt his faith. When he stood firm in his Orthodox faith, the Emperor became angry and ordered to kill him. Theodora, the emperor's wife who was Orthodox in faith, knew about what the Emperor was about to do, so she told the saint to flee to Egypt.

St. Severus escaped to the land of Egypt and that was during the papacy of Pope Timothy III. He wandered around between monasteries and the Egyptian cities in simple monk attire confirming the believers in the Orthodox faith. That made the emperor to incite a severe persecution against the Coptic Church for accepting St. Severus who was fleeing from his face.

He dwelt in the later part of his life in the city of Sakha at a righteous Archon called Doretheos. God performed many miracles by his hands. He departed in the city of Sakha, and his body was relocated later on to the monastery of El-Zugag nearby Alexandria.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-14.title: The Departure of St. Severus, Patriarch of Antioch

06-14.html:
On this day also of the year 546 of the martyrs (830 A.D.), the Holy Father Pope James (Jacob), 50th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was born in the city of Nabaroh. His parents raised him up with a Christian upbringing and taught him the church subjects. When he grew, became a monk in the monastery of St. Macarius in the wilderness of Shiheet. He lived a godly monastic life.

When Pope Mark II departed, they chose him by a consensus for the patriarchate. He was consecrated in the year 819 A.D. He renovated the churches and populated the monasteries. God granted him the working of miracles and signs as raising a child from the dead in the city of Nabaroh.

When he finished his good endeavor, he departed in peace after sitting on the apostolic throne for 10 years and 9 months.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-14.title: The Departure of St. James (Jacob), 50th Patriarch of Alexandria

06-15.html:
On this day the ascetic monk St. Paphnoute departed. This Holy Father became a monk in one of the monasteries of Upper Egypt. He lived a holy life to the point that they looked to him more as an angel than a human. He enjoyed much the company of the blessed spirits of the saints as he had a great favor before God in his prayers. He attracted many to the monastic life.

The grace of God moved him to travel to the inner wilderness to meet the fathers the anchorites and record their biographies. He rose up and walked many days in the wilderness and suffered many hardships on his way. The angel of the Lord appeared to him often to encourage and strengthen him until he finally reached where the fathers the anchorites dwelled. He saw many of them among those well known were Anba Timothy and Anba Nofer (Onnuphrius). He was the one to shroud Anba Nofer and bury him.

He longed for the life of the anchorites and desired to remain there but the saint Anba Nofer told him that this was not the will of God for him. But he had to return to his monastery and to inform the brethren of what he saw and heard for the benefit of the monks and those seeking the path of righteousness. Consequently after the departure of Anba Nofer the palm tree that he fed on its fruits fell down and the spring of water dried up and the cave that he lived in collapsed so St. Paphnoute returned sorrowful.

He persevered in the life of asceticism and worship and finally the angel of the Lord appeared to him and called upon him to depart to the eternal habitations. The brethren gathered around him and listened to many useful sayings from him then delivered up his pure soul.

The blessing of his prayer be with us all. Amen.
06-15.title: The Departure of St. Paphnoute, the Monk

06-15.html:
On this day also the righteous prophet Zechariah the Son of Berechiah, the Son of Iddo, one of the twelve Minor Prophets, was martyred. He was from the tribe of Levi, and was born in the land of Gilead. His father’s name was Berechiah who died young so the prophet was named after his grandfather Iddo.

He was exiled to the land of the Chaldeans. In exile, he prophesied in the 8th month, in the second year of the reign of King Darius about the year 520 B.C. After the king had allowed the men of Judah to return to Jerusalem. The prophet’s message was centered on strengthening the frail determination of the people to behave with the spirit of godliness and rebuild the temple.

He then uncovered the glorious future of Jesus Christ who emanated hope in them after the destruction of Jerusalem and the cities of Judah during the period of exile which lasted 70 years.

He also prophesied about the incarnation of the Word in the midst of Zion. He prophesied also about His triumphant entrance into Jerusalem, selling Him with thirty pieces of silver, the piercing of His hands and feet, the darkness during His crucifixion, piercing Him with the spear, the scattering of the disciples, and His sending of the Holy Spirit.

When the Jews became angry from the admonishing of this prophet they conspired against him and slew him between the temple and the altar. As the Savior had told the scribes and the Pharisees, “that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.”

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-15.title: The Martyrdom of the Righteous Zechariah the Prophet the Son of Berechiah, the Son of Iddo

06-15.html:
Today also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) marks the martyrdom of St. Begoul (Pigol) the priest. This saint was born in Upper Egypt and for his piety and good conduct they ordained him a presbyter. His emphasis was on exhorting the people, teaching them, and confirming them in the faith.

When he heard about the torment of the Christians, he went to Alexandria where he met his namesake the saint Anba Begoul the soldier during his torture. They seized and handed him to the prefect Closianus who tortured then imprisoned him. When Armanius became the governor of Alexandria they brought St. Begoul the priest before him. He confessed the Lord Christ with conviction.

Henceforth, the governor ordered him to be scourged and severely tortured, which he endured with peace and serenity. The Lord performed some miracles by his hands which the governor attributed to witchcraft and told him, “O teacher of magic, why not abandon your witchcraft and worship the gods? For the One that you rely on cannot save you from my hands this time.” Armanius the governor ordered to crush him with the Hinbazeen and then placed him on an iron bed under which hot fire and finally ordered to behead him.

The saint said: “Now my joy has been completed and fulfilled my priesthood, for I have served the Lord for forty years for the sake of this hour.” The swordsman came forward and beheaded him thus he received the crown of martyrdom. A church after his name still exists in the village of Talah west of the city of el-Menia.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-15.title: The Martyrdom of Anba Begoul (Pigol) the Priest

06-15.html:
On this day also the church celebrates the commemoration of the consecration of the church of the forty martyrs who were martyred in Sebaste by the hands of Emperor Licinius. It was the first church that had been built after their names where their bodies were located in Sebaste. St. Basil the Great consecrated it. He also wrote their biographies and established a great feast day for them on this day.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-15.title: The Consecration of the First Church Dedicated for the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste

06-16.html:
On this day the upright St. Elizabeth, mother of St. John the Baptist and the wife of Zacharias the priest, departed. This holy woman was born in Jerusalem to a righteous father called Matthan (Matthew) from the tribe of Levi and from the house of Aaron the priest. Her mother was a pious woman called Sofia.

There was a familial relation between her and the holy Virgin St. Mary for their mothers were related. The Holy Scriptures testified about her and her husband that: "They were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless."

Elizabeth was barren; she and her husband constantly prayed and entreated God to give them an offspring. They persevered in supplicating God for many years until they became well advanced in age. God was slow in answering their prayers for a divine providence till the time that was appointed by God for the incarnation of the Lord Christ the Son of God the Logos. For St. John the Baptist, son of Zacharias and Elizabeth was the angel to prepare the way before Him.

In the fullness of time God sent His angel Gabriel to Zacharias to announce him with the conception of Elizabeth with John and the angel told him what would become of this saint. Elizabeth rejoiced along with her neighbors and relatives.

The Virgin St. Mary visited her to congratulate and serve her during her pregnancy in her old age. When she entered the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth. And it happened, when Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary that the babe leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. Then she spoke out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! But why is granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For indeed as soon as the voice of your greeting sounded in my ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy. Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of those things which were told her from the Lord. And Mary remained with her about three months, and returned to her house.

When Elizabeth full time came for her to be delivered and she brought forth a son. When her neighbors and relatives heard how the Lord had shown great mercy to her they rejoiced with her. The child was called John as was called by the angel.

When Elizabeth completed her days, she departed in peace.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-16.title: The Departure of St. Elizabeth, Mother of St. John the Baptist

06-16.html:
On this day also of the year 1194 of the martyrs (1478 A.D.) Pope Michael III, the 92nd Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This Holy Father was born in Samalut, el-Minya governorate to Christian parents who taught him the Christian subjects. He longed for the monastic life, became a monk in one of the monasteries and lived a godly life.

After the departure of Pope Gabriel VI, the bishops and lay leaders (Archons) unanimously agreed to choose this monk for the patriarchate. He was consecrated on the 13th of Meshir, year 1193 of the martyrs (1477 A.D.). He did not last long on the apostolic throne but only one year and three days then departed in peace. He was buried with great honor in the church of the Virgin, Babylon el-Darag in Old Cairo.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-16.title: The Departure of Pope Michael III, the 92nd Patriarch of Alexandria

06-16.html:
Today also of the year 1639 of the martyrs (1923 A.D.) marks the departure of the Hegumen Michael (Mikhael) el-Behairy, el Muharraqy. He was the disciple of the great saint Anba Abraam bishop of el-Fayyum and el-Giza.

This Holy Father was born in the year 1847 A.D.in the city of Eshneen el-Nasarah. His parents were pious Christians who raised him in a true Christian upbringing that yielded a blessed fruit. He was called el-Behairy in reference to the name of his family (el-Beharrwah) for they were originally from el-Beheira governorate.

When he was twelve years old, his father became seriously ill and was dying. His mother had compassion on him from seeing his father dead and the people crying and mourning over him, so she sent him to the house of a relative. While he was on the roof, he saw the spirit of his father ascending to heaven surrounded by luminous angels praising and singing hymns. He immediately recognized it and shouted saying; “My father … my father.” One of the angels told him ask and pray that your end would be like him.

During this period, he met a monk from el-Muharraq monastery whose name was the Hegumen Tawadros who always talked to him about the nobility of monasticism and the angelic life of the monks. Accordingly he passionately loved virginity and the monastic life which he practiced at home. Later on he went to el-Muharraq monastery and joined it during the time of the Hegumen Bolos el-Dalagawy el-Muharraqy who became later on the great saint Anba Abraam.

He remained in the monastery for a period as a novice and when the abbot of the monastery and the monks saw his meekness and obedience, he was ordained a monk by the name monk Michael (Mikhael). They handed him to a holy old monk called Hegumen Saleeb el-Owlwany to show him the path to the monastic life.

The monk Mikhael grew in piety and asceticism, and everyone loved him. He was ordained a priest in the year 1874 A.D. then Hegumen. Later on he became a father of confession and spiritual guide to all the monks of the monastery.

God granted him the gift of healing the infirm, many sought his prayers and God was glorified through his healing hands. This saint became well known for the virtue of giving and compassion to the needy as his teacher the great saint Anba Abraam. He offered them from the little he had with love and contentment. In the later part of his life he lost his vision however he thanked God and persisted on praying.

After a life full of righteous deeds, holiness, asceticism, compassion, purity and after he practiced and taught by his sayings and deeds, he reposed in the Lord. His age was 76 years old, twenty years in the world and 56 years in the monastery spent in hard monastic struggle elevated him to the rank of the saints.

At the time of his departure, one of the Ethiopian older monks, residing in the monastery, saw his pure spirit ascending to heaven accompanied by angels while singing and praising God. On the feast of his repose, year 1707 of the martyrs (1991 A.D.) and during the papacy of Pope Shenouda III, the 117th Patriarch of Alexandria, his relics were uncovered with great veneration in the presence of 14 bishops. His body was placed in a special shrine in the monastery for the Christ loving people to receive his blessings.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-16.title: The Departure of the Hegumen Michael (Mikhael) el-Behairy, el Muharraqy

06-17.html:
On this day St. Mina the monk was martyred. This saint was born in Akhmim to Christian parents. His father worked in farming. His parents raised him in a true Christian upbringing. Since his youth, his heart was inclined to renounce the world. When he grew, became a monk in one of the monasteries of Akhmim.

For a period of time, he dwelt there in asceticism and worship. Then he went to el-Ashmunain and resided there in a monastery and did not leave it for 16 years.

When the Arabs ruled the country, the saint heard that they resisted and denied the doctrine of the divine incarnation. He took permission from the abbot of the monastery and went to el-Ashmunain. He came before the Arab captain of the soldiers and debated that with him. The saint explained to the captain the validity of his faith and the necessity of the incarnation of the Word of God for the salvation of the world. The son-ship of the Son is not through parental procreation but a son-ship of a special kind as the light proceeds from the Sun.

The captain became enraged and ordered his soldiers to cut the saint into pieces and to throw him into the river thus he received the crown of martyrdom. The believers gathered the pieces of his pure body, shrouded and buried it with great honor.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-17.title: The Martyrdom of St. Mina the Monk

06-17.html:
On this day also was the Consecration of the Church of the martyr St. Castor of Bardanouha. This saint was martyred in Alexandria and when his body arrived to his hometown Bardanouha, all the people went out to receive him. They carried his body with great veneration to his house. After the end of the persecution, they changed his home to a church after his name and was consecrated on this day. Until present time there is a church in Bardanouha after his name.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-17.title: The Consecration of the Church of St. Castor of Bardanouha

06-18.html:
On this day of the year 381 A.D., St. Malatius the Confessor, Patriarch of Antioch, departed. He was consecrated a bishop for Sebaste in the year 357 A.D. He left it because of the rudeness and harshness of its people and lived in solitude nearby the City of Halab in Syria. In the year 360 A.D., he was chosen a patriarch for Antioch.

He was firm in resisting the Arians. When Emperor Constantius, who was Arian, heard that, he exiled him in the same year of his enthronement. The bishops, priests and people convened and wrote to the Emperor asking for the return of their Patriarch.

When the Emperor responded to their request and brought St. Malatius back in the year 362 A.D., he did not cease resisting the Arians. He persisted in teaching the people the true Orthodox faith according to the faith of the council of Nicea. Therefore the emperor exiled him again. In exile, all the exiled Orthodox faithful gathered around him, encouraging and supporting each other. He sent to his flock pastoral epistles to confirm them in the Orthodox faith.

He remained in exile for many years then returned to Antioch in the year 378 A.D. He attended the universal Council of Constantinople in the year 381 A.D. When he finished his good endeavor departed in peace. St. John Chrysostom (Golden Mouthed) praised St. Malatius declaring his greatness and stature for what he suffered from exile and humiliation for the sake of the Orthodox faith.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-18.title: The Departure of St. Malatius the Confessor, Patriarch of Antioch

06-18.html:
On this day also was the consecration of the church of St. Paul the simple, one of the disciples of the great saint Anba Antonius, father of all monks. Paul (Bolos) was a simple farmer from the city of Atfeeh. He got married when he was advanced in age to a young girl.

One day he went home and caught his wife in the act. He left the house and went to the saint Anba Antonius to be a monk under his guidance and become his pupil. Anba Antonius tried to dissuade him from his determination for his old age and the difficulties of the path of monasticism. When he saw his firm determination, he tested him with difficult examinations and hard tests that he successfully passed them all.

When he saw his perseverance, he accepted him. He commended him to establish for himself a cell nearby him. He lived close to him as an obedient disciple in spite of his old age. Because of his simplicity, asceticism and his struggle, God granted him the gift of casting out evil spirits and revealing the thoughts of men.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-18.title: The Consecration of the Church of St. Paul the Simple

06-19.html:
On this day the church commemorates the relocation of the relics of St. Martianus the monk from Athens to Antioch. He was a monk in Antioch and before the end of his life he went to Athens and departed there.

When St. Demetrius was enthroned Patriarch of Antioch, he took on the endeavor of relocating the relics of St. Martianus to Antioch. He sent priests to Athens who carried the pure body with great veneration to Antioch. He placed the body in a sarcophagus for the people to receive his blessings.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-19.title: The Commemoration of the Relocation of the Relics of St. Martianus the Monk to Antioch

06-20.html:
On this day of the year 95 of the martyrs (379 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Peter II, 21st Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This saint was born in Alexandria and was the successor of St. Athanasius the apostolic who was his teacher.

He followed his teacher in his holiness and was refined with his knowledge. When his teacher saw his advancement in godliness, he ordained him a priest and later on ordained him a bishop. Pope Athanasius sent him to Syria to join St Basil the great in resisting some of the heresies that spread there.

When Pope Athanasius felt that his departure drew near, he commended that his disciple Anba Peter succeed him. After the departure of Pope Athanasius, they consecrated him Patriarch in the year 373 A.D. for what he portrayed from godliness and knowledge.

He struggled against the Arians as he learned from his teacher Pope Athanasius. He suffered many hardships from the Arians, who tried many times, to slay him. He had to disappear for two years for the Arians appointed an illegitimate patriarch; nevertheless the people did not accept him. They brought back their father Pope Peter to his throne and he resumed his resistance against the Arians.

When he finished his good endeavor, the Lord willed to repose him from the toil of this world, departed in peace and went to the heavenly church of the first born.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-20.title: The Departure of St. Peter II, 21st Patriarch of Alexandria

06-20.html:
On this day also the saints Basil, Theodore and Timothy, were martyred in the City of Alexandria.

When Emperor Septimius Severus incited the persecution against the Christians many were martyred at his hands in all parts of Egypt. He imprisoned many so the prisons became churches for they heard from them voices of prayers and praises.

These three saints came forward and declared their faith in the Lord Christ and received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-20.title: The Martyrdom of the Saints, Basil, Theodore and Timothy in Alexandria

06-21.html:
The church celebrates on this day the monthly commemoration of the pure Lady St. Mary the Virgin, the Mother of God through whom was the salvation of Adam and his offspring.

Her holy intercession be with us all. Amen.
06-21.title: The Commemoration of the Virgin St. Mary, the Theotokos

06-21.html:
On this day also St. Onesimus, the disciple of the apostle St. Paul, was martyred. He was a slave owned by St. Philemon who was from the prominent Christians of Colosse.

The devil enticed Onesimus’ heart, led him to steal money from his master and fled to Rome. There he heard about the apostle St. Paul. He believed, repented and was baptized at his hands. He served with him as a deacon then sent him back to Colosse. He sent with him an epistle to St. Philemon asking him to accept Onesimus no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother. St. Tychicus accompanied him on this journey. After he received the forgiveness of his master, he returned to Rome.

According to tradition, St. Onesimus later on became the bishop of Berea. After the martyrdom of St. Paul and by the order of the emperor they seized St. Onesimus and exiled him to one of the islands where he taught and baptized its people. When the ruler of the island heard that, he scourged him and ordered to break his legs so he departed and received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-21.title: The Martyrdom of St. Onesimus, the Disciple of the Apostle St. Paul

06-21.html:
On this day also of the year 636 of the martyrs (920 A.D.) the saintly father Pope Gabriel I, the 57th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was born in the village of el-Mayah. He became a monk in the monastery of St. Macarius the great. He loved solitary life and wept much while praying, asking the Lord to save him from the snares of the devil.

When the fame of his virtues became well known, he was chosen patriarch. He was enthroned on the 21st of Pashons, year 625 of the martyrs (909 A.D.) He cared a great deal for the church affairs, and the patriarchal duties did not prevent him from his worship and asceticism.

He spent most of his days in the wilderness and he fought against the flesh and the devil by increasing fasting, watching, prayers and humility. He persevered in this manner of worship, struggling and preaching for 11 years, then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-21.title: The Departure of St. Gabriel I, 57th Patriarch of Alexandria

06-21.html:
Today also marks the departure of St. Zacharias, Bishop of Sakha. He was the son of a scribe called John who left his position and was chosen for the priesthood. He raised his son Zacharias on the Orthodox faith, studying the church and secular subjects.

When he grew up, the Muslim ruler (El-Wazeer) appointed him a scribe in his cabinet. Afterward he agreed with a friend called Ptolemy who was the prefect of the town of Sakha, to leave their work, go to the wilderness to become monks. That coincided with the coming of a monk from the monastery of St. John Colobos (the Short), so they decided to go with him to his monastery. When the ruler (El-Wazeer) knew that, he prevented them. However they left in secret, walking to the wilderness, without knowing their way. They met on their way, by the will of God, a monk who took them to the monastery of St. John (Yehness). When their friends knew that, they took a letter from the Governor to bring them back, but the Lord dispersed their counsel.

As for Zacharias and his friend, they put on the garb of the monks and exerted themselves in much worship. That was during the time of the saints Abba Gawargah (George) and Abba Abraham who were the best guides for them.

When the Bishop of Sakha departed, the people wrote to the father, the Patriarch, asking to consecrate the monk Zacharias a bishop for them. He brought him and ordained him against his will.

This father directed his interest to visiting his flock, exhorting and teaching them. He wrote many commentaries, exhortations, sermons and discourses. He remained on his throne for 30 years, and then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-21.title: The Departure of St. Zacharias, Bishop of Sakha

06-22.html:
On this day St. Maruta, the bishop of Mia-Farkain, from the countries between the two rivers (Mesopotamia), departed. St. Maruta was a knowledgeable and righteous man.

Emperor Theodosius, the great, sent him to Shapur, king of Persia, to negotiate with him the conditions of the truce that they wanted both to sign. King Shapur welcomed him and housed him in a royal palace.

When St. Maruta knew that the king had an infirm daughter, he asked to bring her to him. He prayed over her and she was healed and the King exceedingly rejoiced. When Maruta found favor in the sight of the king, he asked the King to give him the relics of the saints who were martyred in Persia. The saint collected the relics for which he built a church and a great wall around it. Later on, a city was built inside the wall, which was named Maruta.

After the saint had finished his good strife departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-22.title: The Departure of St. Maruta (Marouta) the Bishop

06-23.html:
On this day of the year 19 of the martyrs (303 A.D.), St. Eusebius, son of Basilides the vizier, was martyred.

This saint was one of the great generals of the Roman army who fought in the war against the Persians. During the war, Diocletian abandoned the faith of the Lord Christ and worshiped the idols. When Eusebius returned after the end of the war and knew that, he agreed with his relatives, Abadir, Yustus, Ekladius, and Theodore (Tadros) to confess their faith in the Lord Christ before him.

When the emperor proposed for them to worship his idols, they all refused. The emperor exiled Eusebius to Egypt to be tortured there. He sent him to the governor of Qift (Coptos), who inflicted upon him many tortures; with the Hinbazeen, dismembered him and by beating him severely. However the angel of the Lord healed, strengthened and comforted him.

He saw in the vision of the night, paradise, the mansions of the saints, and the place that had been prepared personally for him and his soul was consoled.

Later on, the Governor ordered to burn him in a fiery furnace prepared for him outside the City of Ahnas (Hnes). The angel of the Lord came down and put out the fire and took St. Eusebius out safely. Finally, the Governor ordered to behead him and he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
06-23.title: The Martyrdom of St. Eusebius, Son of Basilides the Vizier

06-24.html:
On this day of the year 52 of the martyrs (336 A.D.) St. Agapetus, bishop of Synnada, Phrygia, departed. He was born in Cappadocia to Christian parents. His parents raised him up on godliness and piety. When he grew, he served the hermits and learned from them, worship and asceticism.

That was during the time of the infidel emperor Diocletian. Agapetus went to one of the monasteries where he became a monk. When Licinius the governor heard of him, he brought him by force and enlisted him a soldier in the army. This did not prevent him from continuing in his ascetic life and worship rather he greatly increased in his godliness.

Shortly after, Diocletian perished and Constantine the great reigned. When he knew his account, he released him and the saint returned to the place of his asceticism and worship.

The bishop of Synnada heard about him. He brought him and appointed him as his assistant then ordained him a priest. The saint was greatly dedicated in serving the people. When the bishop of Synnada departed, the people chose him as his successor.

He manifested a fiery zeal in shepherding and serving the souls. He persevered in exhorting and teaching his flock. He also took great interest for caring for the poor and needy. The Lord performed by his hands many splendid signs. When he completed his good endeavor, he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
06-24.title: The Departure of St. Agapetus the Bishop

06-24.html:
On this day also was the martyrdom of St. Timothy of Gaza, and St. Matthias of the City of Quos.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
06-24.title: The Martyrdom of St. Timothy and St. Matthias

06-25.html:
On this day of the year 65 A.D. Sts. Philemon, his wife Apphia, and their son Archippus were martyred. They were native of Colosse capital of Phrygia in Asia Minor.
